slides.title: std::remove Behavior
slides.prompt: What does std::remove(v.begin(), v.end(), val) actually do to a vector?
options: It shifts non-matching elements to the front and returns a new logical end iterator without shrinking vector capacity
It immediately erases matching elements and reduces the vector's size()
It deallocates the vector memory for matching elements
slides.correctAnswer: It shifts non-matching elements to the front and returns a new logical end iterator without shrinking vector capacity

slides.title: Erase-Remove Idiom

slides.title: std::replace_if Functionality
slides.prompt: How does std::replace_if operate on a range?
options: Replaces all elements satisfying a predicate with a specified new value
Replaces elements only if they are equal to zero
Swaps matching elements with another container
slides.correctAnswer: Replaces all elements satisfying a predicate with a specified new value

slides.title: std::generate vs std::fill
slides.prompt: What is the key difference between std::fill and std::generate?
options: std::fill assigns a constant value; std::generate assigns values returned by calling a generator function/lambda
std::generate works only on dynamic arrays
slides.correctAnswer: std::fill assigns a constant value; std::generate assigns values returned by calling a generator function/lambda
